            <td style="WIDTH: 94px">
              <div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font color="#1f497d" size="5" style="FONT-SIZE: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: arial"><a name="Item1">Item 1.</a></font></font></div>
            </td>
            <td width="888">
              <div align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 14pt; COLOR: #1f497d; FONT-FAMILY: arial, sans-serif">Business</font></div>
            </td>

    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 15.95pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #003366; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Overview</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">FPIC
Insurance Group, Inc. (&#8220;FPIC&#8221;) was formed in a reorganization of First
Professionals Insurance Company, Inc., formerly named Florida Physicians
Insurance Company, Inc. (&#8220;First Professionals&#8221;), in 1996.&#160;&#160;We operate
in the medical professional liability (&#8220;MPL&#8221;) insurance sector of the property
and casualty insurance industry as an insurance carrier.&#160;&#160;Our primary
insurance products provide protection for physicians, dentists and other
healthcare providers as individual practitioners or as members of practice
groups.&#160;&#160;Our insurance protects policyholders against losses arising
from professional liability claims and the related defense costs with respect to
injuries alleged to have been caused by medical error or
malpractice.&#160;&#160;Professional corporations share in the limits of
liability under a physician&#8217;s or dentist&#8217;s policy and optional coverage is
available to purchase a separate limit of liability for a professional
corporation under an insured&#8217;s MPL policy.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Unless
the context otherwise requires, the terms<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">&#160;</font>&#8220;we,&#8221; &#8220;our,&#8221; &#8220;us,&#8221; the
&#8220;Company,&#8221; and &#8220;FPIC&#8221; as used in this report refer to FPIC Insurance Group, Inc.
and its subsidiaries.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">In
November 2009, we acquired Advocate, MD Financial Group, Inc. (&#8220;Advocate,
MD&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Pursuant to the terms of the agreement, First Professionals
acquired all of the issued and outstanding stock of Advocate, MD, which then
became a wholly owned subsidiary of First Professionals.&#160;&#160;Advocate, MD
is the fourth largest provider of MPL insurance in Texas and also writes MPL
insurance in Mississippi.&#160;&#160;For additional information, see <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Item 7.&#160;&#160;Management&#8217;s
Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of
Operations.</font>&#160;&#160;We intend to operate Advocate, MD through its
current management team and facilities in Austin, Texas.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">We are
the largest provider of MPL insurance in Florida, the fourth largest provider in
Texas and have top five market positions in Georgia and Arkansas.&#160;&#160;In
all, we currently write MPL insurance in 13 states and are licensed to write in
32 states.&#160;&#160;Based on 2008 premiums reported by SNL Financial LC (the
most recent calendar year data available to us), Florida and Texas are the fifth
and eighth largest markets, respectively, for MPL insurance in the United States
in terms of direct premiums written.&#160;&#160;We focus on selected markets
where we believe we have advantages in terms of our market knowledge,
well-established reputation, meaningful market presence and
resources.</font></div>

December 31, 2009, we employed 165 people.&#160;&#160;Our employees are not
covered by a collective bargaining agreement.&#160;&#160;We believe our
relationships with our employees are very important and further believe that our
significant number of long-term employees is indicative of good employee
relations.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; COLOR: #003366">Business Strategy </font></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">As a
leading provider of MPL insurance, we strive to provide superior products and
services to our policyholders, while providing long-term value for our
shareholders.&#160;&#160;We believe we have competitive advantages in our core
markets resulting from our deep expertise, strong relationships and market
positions.&#160;&#160;Our physician-oriented culture and emphasis on providing
outstanding policyholder service have helped us maintain consistent policyholder
retention in excess of 90 percent.&#160;&#160;In addition to our commitment to
our policyholders, our goal is to consistently achieve attractive results for
our shareholders.&#160;&#160;Our business strategy focuses on maintaining a
financially strong, stable and consistently profitable organization while
enhancing shareholder value by adhering to the following core
principles:</font></div>

disciplined growth.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline">&#160;&#160;We believe
that pursuing disciplined growth and prudent expansion&#160;is critical to
sustained profitability over the long-term.&#160;&#160;We systematically assess
opportunities for disciplined growth in the MPL insurance marketplace, including
organic growth in our core markets, entrance into new markets, logical
extensions of our current business and acquisitions of other MPL insurers (such
as Advocate, MD) or MPL books of business.&#160;&#160;We continue to see and
assess growth opportunities in our core markets, which are presented to us as a
result of our long-standing relationships in the medical and agent communities,
our expertise and our strong market and capital positions.&#160;&#160;In
addition, as a complement to our core underwriting operations, we have developed
an initiative to provide management and related services to groups and
organizations that choose not to purchase insurance from the traditional
insurance markets.&#160;&#160;Market conditions in the states where we operate
have stabilized in recent years, but remain highly
competitive.&#160;&#160;Additionally, as a result of significantly improved loss
trends, pricing has declined in recent years, particularly in our Florida and
Texas markets.&#160;&#160;This lower rate environment combined with our
commitment to disciplined underwriting and pricing will continue to make organic
revenue and policyholder growth challenging in the near term.&#160;&#160;We
remain focused on new business opportunities that are consistent with our
strategic objectives.</font></font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Through
February 22, 2010, we have repurchased an additional 112,129 shares on a
settlement date basis, under our Rule 10b5-1 plan, at an aggregate cost of $4.2
million, or $37.84 per share, and had remaining authority from our Board of
Directors to repurchase 668,245 more shares as of that date.&#160;&#160;We will
continue to evaluate additional stock repurchases in light of market conditions,
capital requirements and our financial and business outlook.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt">

        <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
        <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; COLOR: #003366; FONT-STYLE: italic">Focusing
on key geographic markets.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; COLOR: #003366">&#160;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline">We target selected market areas where we believe we can
establish a meaningful presence and leverage local market knowledge and
experience.&#160;&#160;We believe that the ability to manage our business
effectively and compete within the unique environment of each state is critical
to our success.</font></font></div>
      </div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; COLOR: #003366; FONT-STYLE: italic">Maintaining
disciplined underwriting and pricing.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline">We maintain a disciplined focus on selecting appropriate
risks and pricing those risks in order to achieve our financial
objectives.&#160;&#160;In the face of declining premium rates and increased
competition in our core markets, it will continue to be important for us to
maintain appropriate pricing and risk selection.</font></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; COLOR: #003366; FONT-STYLE: italic">Effectively
managing loss costs and operational expenses.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline">&#160;&#160;In addition to prudent risk selection, we
manage our loss costs through effective claims handling and risk management
initiatives.&#160;&#160;We seek to minimize our incidence of claims by offering
our insureds risk management programs that are designed to assist them in
successfully managing their <font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial">individual</font> risk
factors.&#160;&#160;Once a claim has been made, we work to effectively manage
the claim to an appropriate resolution.&#160;&#160;We strive to maintain an
efficient operating cost structure while delivering a high level of service to
our customers.</font></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; COLOR: #003366; FONT-STYLE: italic">Recruiting
and retaining experienced management</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; COLOR: #003366">.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline">&#160;&#160;We have an experienced management team with
diverse expertise in insurance, accounting, finance and legal
disciplines.&#160;&#160;Our management team has an <font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial">average</font> of more than 22 years
of experience in the insurance industry and professions serving the insurance
industry.&#160;&#160;We establish performance expectations and measure
performance of our management team consistent with our strategies for creating
shareholder value.</font></font></div>

reinsure portions of our business, principally through our excess of loss
reinsurance program.&#160;&#160;Although reinsurance does not legally discharge
us from our obligations to policyholders as the primary insurer, it does make
the reinsurers liable to us to the extent of the risks ceded.&#160;&#160;The
placement of reinsurance with a number of individual companies and syndicates
assists in mitigating the concentration of credit risk under our excess of loss
reinsurance program.&#160;&#160;We monitor the financial condition and
creditworthiness of our reinsurers periodically and use reinsurance brokers and
intermediaries to assist in the process of the placement of our
reinsurance.&#160;&#160;Most of our reinsurers are rated A or better by A.M.
Best.&#160;&#160;Reinsurers that are not authorized or accredited by applicable
state insurance departments are required to provide collateral in the form of an
irrevocable letter of credit or to provide investment securities held in a trust
account to secure their respective balances due.&#160;&#160;The following table
summarizes our ceded premiums written by program.</font></div>

Insurance Group, Inc.</font></div>
          <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 15.95pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Annual

            </div><br></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Our
principal insurance subsidiary, First Professionals, was established by Florida
physicians and has served the Florida market for more than 30
years.&#160;&#160;In Florida, we are endorsed by the Florida Medical Association
and the Florida Dental Association, 21 county medical societies and 9 state
specialty societies.&#160;&#160;We also continue to develop relationships with
organized medicine in other markets, including medical societies in Texas and
Georgia.&#160;&#160;Our endorsements, however, do not require us to accept
applicants for insurance who do not meet our underwriting
criteria.&#160;&#160;Our years in the Florida market have enabled us to develop
extensive resources in the state and a deep understanding of the market and its
regulatory and judicial environments.&#160;&#160;We believe this market
knowledge provides us with competitive advantages in terms of underwriting,
pricing, claims management and policyholder service.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #003366; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Underwriting</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">We
believe that prudent risk selection is also integral to our
success.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, we focus on a wide range of underwriting
factors, including the individual professional&#8217;s practice environment, training,
claims history, professional reputation, medical specialty and geographic
location of practice.&#160;&#160;We underwrite professionals on an individual
basis, whether they practice individually or as a member of a
group.&#160;&#160;We generally require board certification or board eligibility
from an appropriate American specialty board as a prerequisite for
coverage.&#160;&#160;We believe that our extensive market knowledge provides us
with a competitive advantage in establishing appropriate pricing and risk
selection.&#160;&#160;Within our chosen markets, we do not manage our business
to achieve specified market share goals.&#160;&#160;Rather, we seek to maximize
our profitability by competing for quality business based on factors other than
price alone.</font></div>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">99
percent of the policies we offer are on a claims-made basis, where only claims
reported to us prior to the cancellation or expiration of the policy period are
covered.&#160;&#160;We believe our claims-made approach allows us to estimate
our loss exposure and price our coverage more accurately than with policies
written on an occurrence basis generally, where losses may be reported for a
number of years after a policy&#8217;s coverage period.&#160;&#160;We offer occurrence
policies in selected markets where occurrence coverage is widely available and
were we believe we can reasonably estimate claim experience and establish
appropriate rates.&#160;&#160;Tail policies, which are written on an occurrence
basis, are offered to existing policyholders who meet certain requirements upon
the non-renewal or cancellation of their policy, or upon their death, disability
or retirement from practice.&#160;&#160;In our largest market, Florida, many
physicians and other medical professionals have responded to increasing MPL
insurance premiums by purchasing lower coverage limits.&#160;&#160;As a result,
our purchased policy limits in Florida are lower on average than is typically
the case in many other markets.&#160;&#160;Similarly, in Texas purchased policy
limits tend to be lower.&#160;&#160;The following table shows the distribution
of the policy limits of our insured Florida physicians:</font></div>

            <td valign="bottom" width="1%" style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: arial, sans-serif">&#160;</font></td>
            <td valign="bottom" width="18%" style="TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: arial, sans-serif">70%</font></td>

          </tr><tr>
            <td align="left" valign="bottom" width="52%" style="PADDING-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 446pt">
              <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: arial, sans-serif">$0.5
      million per loss or less</font></div>
            </td>
            <td valign="bottom" width="1%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: arial, sans-serif">&#160;</font></td>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">We
believe lower policy limits prevalent in our primary markets, among other
things, generally contributes to reduced volatility in our loss severity
relative to other markets where higher insured limits are
prevalent.&#160;&#160;A lower policy limit distribution, however, may also
result in an increase in exposure to extra-contractual obligations ("ECO") and
claims in excess of policy limits (&#8220;XPL&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Generally, our excess of
loss reinsurance programs include coverage for such claims, subject to the
coverage limits described in <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Note 9, Reinsurance</font> to the
consolidated financial statements included elsewhere herein.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #003366; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Claims
Management</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">We seek
to aggressively defend non-meritorious claims and expeditiously resolve
meritorious claims in order to lower our overall loss costs and to&#160;manage
our ECO and XPL exposure.&#160;&#160;Our claims management philosophy also seeks
to minimize the number of claims settled with an indemnity payment, as
appropriate, and to effectively manage defense and other claim
costs.&#160;&#160;In furtherance of our claims strategy, we employ personnel
with significant MPL claims experience and training and we utilize a select
network of defense attorneys to assist us in executing our claims management
philosophy.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #003366; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Risk
Management</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">We also
provide our insureds with comprehensive risk management services designed to
heighten their awareness of situations giving rise to potential liability, to
educate them on ways to improve administration and operation of their medical
practices and to assist them in implementing risk management processes<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">.&#160;&#160;</font>In addition, we
conduct risk management surveys for clinics and large medical groups to help
improve their practice procedures.&#160;&#160;Complete reports of these surveys
that specify areas of the insured&#8217;s medical or dental practice that may need
attention are provided to the policyholder on a confidential
basis.&#160;&#160;We author three risk management newsletters, contribute
multiple articles to professional journals and provide comprehensive risk
management reference materials to our policyholders.&#160;&#160;We also
participate in periodic seminars on risk management to medical societies and
other groups.&#160;&#160;These educational offerings are designed to increase
risk awareness and the effectiveness of loss prevention and also strengthen our
relationship with our customers.</font></div>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #003366; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Industry
Overview</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">According
to the latest calendar year data published by SNL Financial LC, the MPL
insurance market in the United States totaled $11.1 billion in direct premiums
written for the year ended December 31, 2008, a decrease of 3.7 percent over the
prior year.&#160;&#160;The financial performance of the property and casualty
insurance industry, and of the MPL insurance sector, has tended to fluctuate in
cyclical patterns characterized by periods of greater competition in pricing and
underwriting terms and conditions (a soft insurance market) followed by periods
of capacity shortage and lesser competition (a hard insurance
market).</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">We are
currently operating under soft market conditions, with significant competition
and premium rates continuing to moderate downward following several years of
overall favorable claims trends, including lower levels of claim
frequency.&#160;&#160;While we currently expect claim frequency to remain well
below levels seen in 2003 and prior years, an upward trend in claim frequency
going forward is possible.&#160;&#160;In response to favorable claim trends, our
Florida insurance subsidiaries implemented the premium rate reductions shown in
the table below from 2006 to 2008.&#160;&#160;Further rate changes may be
implemented if actuarially warranted.&#160;&#160;Additionally, we may face
pressure from insurance regulatory authorities to implement further rate changes
from time to time.&#160;&#160;In recent years, the Florida Office of Insurance
Regulation (the &#8220;Florida OIR&#8221;) has sought to minimize premium rates in property
and casualty insurance generally, including in the MPL insurance line based on
its assessment of improved claims trends.&#160;&#160;Although, there were no
rate changes in Florida with an effective date in 2009, with the exception of
the factor in our rate filings to recoup assessments levied by the Florida OIR,
we expect this challenging market environment, with continued pressure on
premium rates and new business prospects to continue at least through
2010.&#160;&#160;The Florida premium rate changes and effective dates since
January 1, 2006 are shown below:</font></div>

      respect to assessments levied by the Florida OIR as a result of the
      insolvency of the insurance subsidiaries of Poe Financial
      Group.&#160;&#160;For additional information on the assessments levied in
      2006 and 2007 by the Florida OIR, see <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Note 19, Commitments and
      Contingencies </font>to the consolidated financial statements included
      elsewhere herein.</font></div>
              </td>
            </tr><tr>
              <td align="left" valign="top" width="7%">
                <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: arial, sans-serif">(3)</font></div>
              </td>
              <td align="left" valign="top" width="71%">
                <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: arial, sans-serif">The
      rate decrease was 11.0 percent before giving effect to the 2006
      assessments discussed above.</font></div>
              </td>
            </tr><tr>
              <td align="left" valign="top" width="7%">
                <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: arial, sans-serif">(4)</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font color="#003366" size="2"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Insurance
Ratings</font></font></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font size="2">&#160;</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Insurance-specific
ratings represent the opinion of rating agencies regarding the financial
strength of an insurance company and its capacity to meet its insurance
obligations.&#160;&#160;These ratings are based on factors more relevant to
policyholders, agents and intermediaries than investors and are not specifically
directed toward the protection of investors.&#160;&#160;They are not
recommendations to buy, sell or hold a company&#8217;s securities.&#160;&#160;The
significance of individual agencies and their ratings vary among different
users.&#160;&#160;Our primary rating organizations are A.M. Best and Fitch and
represent the only rating agencies that we have engaged to provide a rating on
an interactive basis.&#160;&#160;Other organizations that may rate us develop
their ratings independently using publicly available data and without consulting
with us; these ratings are generally consumer-oriented and involuntary on our
part.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">An
insurance company&#8217;s rating, and particularly its A.M. Best rating, is a
potential source of competitive advantage or disadvantage in the
marketplace.&#160;&#160;In addition, certain independent agents and brokers may
establish a minimum A.M. Best rating for participation in a potential
market.&#160;&#160;The significance of the A.M. Best rating to a given company
varies depending upon the products involved, customers, agents, competition and
market conditions.&#160;&#160;In addition, the significance of the A.M. Best
rating may vary from state to state.&#160;&#160;Our insurance subsidiaries have
a group financial strength rating from A.M. Best of A-(Excellent) with a stable
outlook, which is within the secure range of available ratings and represents
the fourth highest of 16 rating levels.&#160;&#160;Our insurance subsidiaries
have a group insurer financial strength rating of A- (Strong) from Fitch, which
represents the third highest of nine rating levels.</font></div>

agencies, all of which represent more than one company, we face competition
among our own agents.&#160;&#160;We also believe that a significant portion of
the MPL insurance market will continue to be served by alternative risk
arrangements outside the traditional insurance marketplace.&#160;&#160;We
compete within this environment on the basis of our leadership position in our
core markets and our relationships with the medical and professional communities
we serve.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">We
believe that the principal competitive factors affecting our business are
service, reputation and price, and that we are competitive in all of these
areas.&#160;&#160;We enjoy particularly strong name recognition in Florida, our
largest market, by virtue of having been organized by, and initially operated
for the benefit of, Florida physicians.&#160;&#160;The services offered to our
insureds, as well as the healthcare community in general, are intended to
promote name recognition and to maintain and improve loyalty among our
insureds.&#160;&#160;MPL insurance underwritten by First Professionals has the
exclusive endorsement of the Florida Medical Association and the Florida Dental
Association.&#160;&#160;We are also endorsed by various county and state medical
societies in Florida, Georgia and Texas.&#160;&#160;In general, local carriers
that have been able to maintain strong customer loyalty dominate the MPL market
in their respective states.&#160;&#160;We seek to grow our position in other
chosen markets by targeting certain specialties and quality
business.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #003366; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Insurance
Regulation</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Each of
our insurance subsidiaries is regulated at the state level.&#160;&#160;The state
insurance departments of Florida, Texas and Missouri, where our insurance
subsidiaries are domiciled, are our primary regulators.&#160;&#160;Our insurance
subsidiaries are also subject to regulation in other states where they do
business.&#160;&#160;State insurance laws also regulate us as an insurance
holding company.&#160;&#160;Our insurance subsidiaries are required to register
and furnish information regarding operations, management and financial condition
to state insurance departments.&#160;&#160;State insurance departments
periodically perform financial examinations and market conduct examinations of
the insurance companies they regulate.&#160;&#160;They also require disclosure
or approval of material transactions, such as dividends above certain levels
from our insurance subsidiaries to the holding company.&#160;&#160;All
transactions within the holding company structure involving our insurance
subsidiaries must also be fair and reasonable to our insurance
subsidiaries.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Except
as described below, Florida insurance laws do not allow any person to acquire,
directly or indirectly, five percent or more of the voting securities of a
Florida insurance company without the prior written approval of the Florida
OIR.&#160;&#160;Any purchaser of five percent or more of our common stock is
presumed to have acquired a similar level of control of our insurance
subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;Instead of obtaining prior approval, a purchaser of
more than five percent, but not more than ten percent, of a Florida insurance
company&#8217;s voting securities may file a disclaimer of affiliation and control
with the Florida OIR.&#160;&#160;Similar laws exist in Texas and Missouri,
except that the approval threshold is ten percent or more.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">The
primary purpose or mission of insurance regulation is the protection of
policyholders.&#160;&#160;State insurance laws generally delegate broad
regulatory powers to insurance departments, including the power to grant and
revoke licenses, to approve policy forms and premium rates, to regulate trade
practices, to establish minimum capital and surplus levels for companies, to
prescribe or permit required statutory accounting and financial reporting rules,
and to prescribe the types and amounts of investments permitted.</font></div>

          <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 15.95pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Annual

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Insurance
companies are required to file detailed annual reports in each state in which
they do business.&#160;&#160;The financial statements contained in such reports
are prepared using regulatory accounting principles and are referred to in the
insurance industry as statutory-basis financial statements.&#160;&#160;Statutory
accounting principles represent a comprehensive basis of accounting that is
different from accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of
America ("GAAP"), and consequently the accounting practices used by our
insurance subsidiaries in their regulatory financial statements are different in
certain material respects from the accounting policies used in preparing the
consolidated financial statements included in this report.&#160;&#160;The
National Association of Insurance Commissioners (the &#8220;NAIC&#8221;) has adopted the
Codification of Statutory Accounting Principles (the &#8220;NAIC
Codification&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The NAIC Codification became applicable to all
statutory-basis financial statements issued after January 1,
2001.&#160;&#160;While the NAIC Codification represents the official guidance on
the statutory-basis of accounting, each individual state and insurance
department continues to have the discretion to modify this guidance or establish
its own statutory accounting principles for insurance companies.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Our
insurance subsidiaries are subject to assessment by the insurance guaranty
associations in the states in which they conduct business for the provision of
funds necessary for the settlement of covered claims against insolvent
insurers.&#160;&#160;Generally, these associations can assess insurers on the
basis of written premiums in their particular states.&#160;&#160;In November
2009, the Florida OIR levied an assessment of 0.8 percent on all 2008 Florida
property and casualty direct premiums written (an assessment of $1.2 million in
our case).&#160;&#160;The Florida OIR also levied similar assessments in 2006
and 2007. Under Florida law, our insurance subsidiaries are entitled to recoup
insurance guaranty fund assessments from their Florida policyholders and will
continue to do so until fully recovered.&#160;&#160;For additional information
on these assessments see <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Note
19, Commitments and Contingencies </font>to the consolidated financial
statements included elsewhere herein.</font></div>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">In
addition to standard guaranty fund assessments, the Florida, Texas and Missouri
legislatures could also levy special assessments to settle claims caused by
certain catastrophic losses.&#160;&#160;No such special assessments for
catastrophic losses were made in 2009, 2008 or 2007.&#160;&#160;MPL policies
have been exempted from assessment by the Florida Hurricane Catastrophe Fund
until the expiration of this exemption on May 31, 2010.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Discussions
continue in the United States Congress concerning health care reform as well as
the future of the McCarran-Ferguson Act, which exempts the "business of
insurance" from most federal laws, including anti-trust laws, to the extent such
business is subject to state regulation.&#160;&#160;It is not possible to
predict the effect on our operations of any health care reform, or repeal,
modification, or any narrowed interpretation of the McCarran-Ferguson
Act.&#160;</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #003366; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Tort
Reform</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">A
number of the states in which we operate, including Florida, Texas, Georgia,
Arkansas, and Missouri, have passed various medical malpractice tort reform
measures.&#160;&#160;For instance, beginning in 2003, Florida enacted a series
of laws and adopted a series of constitutional amendments that provide for,
among other things, a $0.5 million cap on non-economic damages under certain
circumstances, certain modifications to bad faith statutes, limitations on fees
to plaintiffs&#8217; attorneys, and abolition of joint and several liability in
medical malpractice actions.&#160;&#160;Similarly, Texas has, among other
things, placed caps on non-economic damages (a $0.25 million in the aggregate
recoverable from all individual defendants and a $0.5 million in the aggregate
recoverable from all institutions) and abolished joint and several
liability.&#160;&#160;In general, we believe that these reforms have provided an
additional level of stability to the MPL insurance market and have contributed
to the decline in frequency of claims since enactment.&#160;&#160;The Florida
cap on non-economic damages has been held, subject to appeal, by one Florida
appellate court to be unconstitutional as applied to &#8220;straddle cases&#8221; in that
jurisdiction (cases involving claims made after the effectiveness of the cap for
alleged injuries that occurred prior to the effectiveness of the cap) and has
been challenged in the Florida appellate court of another
jurisdiction.&#160;&#160;We expect these cases ultimately to be decided by the
Florida Supreme Court.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #003366; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Because
of our significant concentration in MPL insurance, our profitability may be
adversely affected by negative developments and cyclical changes in that
industry.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Substantially
all of our revenues are generated from our involvement in the MPL insurance
industry.&#160;&#160;Because of our concentration in this line of business,
negative developments in the business or economic, competitive or legal
environments or regulatory conditions affecting the MPL insurance industry,
broadly or in our markets, could have a negative effect on our profitability and
would have a more pronounced effect on us compared to more diversified
companies.&#160;&#160;The MPL insurance industry historically is cyclical in
nature, characterized by periods of severe price competition and excess
underwriting capacity (a soft market) followed by periods of high premium rates
and shortages of underwriting capacity (a hard market).&#160;&#160;We are
currently operating under soft market conditions, with significant competition
and premium rates continuing to moderate downward following several years of
overall favorable claims trends.&#160;&#160;During 2006 through 2009, premium
rates declined in our core Florida market, primarily as a result of improved
claims results.&#160;&#160;We cannot predict how market conditions will continue
to change, or the manner in which, or the extent to which, any such changes may
adversely impact our business or profitability.&#160;&#160;We anticipate,
however, that the current soft market conditions will continue at least through
2010.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">We
compete with specialty insurers and in some cases, alternative risk
arrangements, whose activities are limited to regional and local markets, as
well as other large national property and casualty insurance companies that
write MPL insurance.&#160;&#160;Our competitors include companies that have
substantially greater financial resources and higher financial strength ratings
than we have, companies, particularly mutual insurers, reciprocals, risk
retention groups or trusts, that may have lower return on capital objectives
than we have, and start-up companies aggressively seeking market
share.&#160;&#160;We also face competition from other insurance companies for
the services and allegiance of independent agents and brokers, on whose services
we depend in marketing our insurance products.&#160;&#160;Increased competition
could adversely affect our ability to attract and retain business at adequate
prices and reduce our profits, which could have a material adverse effect on our
financial condition, results of operations or cash flows.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #003366; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Our
geographic concentration means that our performance may be affected by economic,
regulatory and demographic conditions of states in which we
operate.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Our
business is affected by general economic conditions in the markets in which we
operate, which in turn may be affected by national general economic
conditions.&#160;&#160;Because our business is concentrated in a limited number
of markets, particularly Florida and Texas, adverse developments that are
limited to a geographic area in which we do business may have a
disproportionately greater affect on us than they would have if we were less
geographically concentrated.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #003366; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Our
success depends on our ability to underwrite risks accurately and to price our
products accordingly.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">The
nature of the insurance business is such that pricing must be determined before
the underlying costs are fully known.&#160;&#160;This requires significant
reliance on estimates and assumptions in setting prices.&#160;&#160;If we fail
to assess accurately the risks that we assume, we may fail to charge adequate
premium rates, which could impact our profitability and have a material adverse
effect on our financial condition, results of operations or cash
flows.&#160;&#160;Our ability to assess our policyholder risks and to price our
products accurately is subject to a number of risks and uncertainties,
including, but not limited to:</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; COLOR: #003366">Our results and financial condition may
be affected by our failure to establish adequate loss and</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; COLOR: #003365; FONT-FAMILY: Arial-BoldMT, sans-serif">
LAE reserves or by reductions in favorable development of prior year
reserves.</font></font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Our
liability for losses and LAE (also referred to as our loss and LAE reserves) is
our largest liability and represents the financial statement item most sensitive
to estimation and judgment.&#160;&#160;In developing our estimates of losses and
LAE, we evaluate and consider actuarial projection techniques based on our
assessment of facts and circumstances then known, historical loss experience
data and estimates of anticipated trends.&#160;&#160;This process assumes that
past experience, adjusted for the effects of current developments, changes in
operations and anticipated trends, constitutes an appropriate basis for
predicting future events.&#160;&#160;While we believe that our loss and LAE
reserves are appropriate, to the extent that such reserves prove to be
inadequate or excessive in the future, we would adjust them and incur a charge
or credit to earnings, as the case may be, in the period the reserves are
adjusted.&#160;&#160;Any such adjustment could have a material impact on our
financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.&#160;&#160;In
addition, our results in recent years have benefited from the recognition of
favorable development of prior year reserves.&#160;&#160;Since our loss and LAE
reserves represent our largest financial statement item subject to estimation
and judgment, there can be no assurance that our estimates will not change in
the future.&#160;&#160;For additional information on our loss and LAE reserves,
see <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Item 7. Management&#8217;s
Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of
Operations.</font></font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #003366; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Our
exposure to claims for extra-contractual obligations and losses in excess of
policy limits and the unpredictability of court decisions could have a material
adverse impact on our financial condition, results of operations or cash
flows.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font color="#000000" style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: normal; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial">Within the Florida market for MPL insurance in particular, the
magnitude of payments for extra-contractual liability and losses in excess of
policy limits (commonly referred to as &#8220;bad faith&#8221; claims) has increased in
recent years and is expected to continue to be a significant source of
uncertainty.&#160;&#160;Our policy to aggressively defend claims made against
our insureds that we consider unwarranted or claims where reasonable settlement
cannot be achieved, and the unpredictability of court decisions, may increase
such exposure.&#160;&#160;An award against us for extra-contractual liability or
a significant jury award, or series of awards, against one or more of our
insureds could ultimately result in the payment by us of potentially significant
amounts in excess of the related policy limits, reserves and reinsurance
coverage and could have a material adverse impact on our financial condition,
results of operations or cash flows.</font></div>

are heavily regulated by the states in which we operate and are subject to
legislative initiatives, regulatory oversight and, indirectly, to pressure from
consumer groups and representatives (including the statutorily appointed Florida
Insurance Consumer Advocate) and others, that may affect the adequacy of our
premium rates; and we may be limited in the way in which we
operate.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">
        <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font color="#000000" style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: normal; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial">Regulation may mandate undesired premium rate changes or may
impede or impose burdensome conditions on premium rate changes or other actions
that we may otherwise intend to take in order to maintain or enhance our
operating results. Our premium rates are also subject to legislative action,
regulatory oversight and, indirectly, to pressure from consumer groups and
representatives (including the statutorily appointed Florida Insurance Consumer
Advocate) and others. In recent years, the Florida OIR has sought to minimize
premium rates in property and casualty insurance generally, including in the MPL
insurance line based on its assessment of improved claims trends. The impact of
any future adverse legislative, regulatory or other such actions on our premium
rates or the way in which we operate, could adversely impact our financial
condition, results of operations and cash flows.</font></div>
      </div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #003366; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">&#160;</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #003366; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Judicial
and legislative review of tort reforms could negatively affect our
operations.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Tort
reforms are generally intended to restrict the ability of a plaintiff to recover
damages by imposing one or more limitations, including, limiting types of claims
that may be heard in court, limiting the amount or types of damages, shortening
the period of time to make a claim, and limiting venue or court
selection.&#160;&#160;Certain states in which we do business have enacted tort
reforms, including Florida and Texas, which have enacted significant MPL
insurance reforms since 2003.&#160;&#160;The constitutionality of certain
Florida tort reforms, related to caps on non-economic damages, is currently
being challenged in at least two Florida courts (one of which has ruled, subject
to appeal, that this cap cannot be applied to so-called &#8220;straddle cases&#8221; in
which the alleged injury occurred prior to the effectiveness of the cap but a
claim against the medical provider concerning the alleged injury is commenced
after the effective date of the cap), and there can be no assurance that tort
reform measures will ultimately be upheld by Florida courts or in any other
state where challenged.&#160;&#160;In addition, we anticipate that trial lawyer
and other groups will continue legislative lobbying efforts to weaken or
overturn existing tort reforms and to block further reforms.</font></div>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #003366; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Our
revenues and financial results may fluctuate with interest rates, investment
results and developments in the securities markets.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">The
fair value of our investment holdings is affected by general economic conditions
and changes in the financial and credit markets, and we rely on the investment
income produced by our investment portfolio to contribute to our
profitability.&#160;&#160;Changes in interest rates and credit quality may
result in fluctuations in the income derived from, the valuation of, and in the
case of declines in credit quality, payment defaults on, our fixed-income
securities.&#160;&#160;In addition, deteriorating economic conditions could
impact the value of our equity securities.&#160;&#160;Such conditions could give
rise to significant realized and unrealized investment losses or the impairment
of securities deemed other-than-temporary.&#160;&#160;These changes could have a
material adverse effect on our financial condition, results of operations or
cash flows.&#160;&#160;Our investment portfolio is also subject to credit and
cash flow risk, including risks associated with our investments in asset-backed
and mortgage-backed securities.&#160;&#160;Because our investment portfolio is
the largest component of our consolidated assets and a multiple of our
shareholders&#8217; equity, adverse changes in economic conditions could result in
other-than-temporary impairments that are material to our financial condition
and operating results.&#160;&#160;Such economic changes could arise from overall
changes in the financial markets or specific changes to industries, companies or
municipalities in which we maintain investment holdings.&#160;&#160;As of
December 31, 2009, we had gross unrealized investment gains and losses of $24.3
million and $6.3 million, respectively, in our investment
portfolio.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #003366; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">We
are subject to assessment by state insurance guaranty associations.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">State
insurance guaranty associations or other insurance regulatory bodies may assess
us, generally on the basis of insurance written in their states, for the
purposes of funding the unpaid claims and policyholder benefits of insolvent
insurers or to cover catastrophes in their states.&#160;&#160;Between 2006 and
2009, we were assessed an aggregate of $14.8 million (including $1.2 million in
2009) by the Florida OIR at the request of the Florida Insurance Guaranty
Association with respect to the insolvency of property and casualty insurance
companies operating in Florida.&#160;&#160;There can be no assurance that we
will not be subject to additional assessments with respect to insolvencies and
such additional assessments could adversely impact our financial condition,
results of operations and cash flows.&#160;&#160;Under Florida law, our
insurance subsidiaries are entitled to recoup insurance guaranty fund
assessments from their Florida policyholders and will continue to do so until
fully recovered.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">

          <div style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left">
            <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">

            <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 15.95pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 14pt; COLOR: #003366; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, serif">FPIC
Insurance Group, Inc.</font></div>
            <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 15.95pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Annual

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #003366; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">&#160;</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">
        <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #003366; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">If
market conditions cause reinsurance to be more costly or unavailable, we may be
required to bear increased risks or reduce the level of our underwriting
commitments.</font></div>
        <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">As part
of our overall risk management strategy, we purchase reinsurance for significant
levels of risk underwritten by our insurance subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;Market
conditions beyond our control determine the availability and cost of the
reinsurance we purchase, which may affect the level of our business and
profitability.&#160;&#160;If we were unable to renew our expiring coverage or to
obtain new reinsurance coverage, our net exposure to risk would increase or, if
we were unwilling to bear an increase in net risk exposures we may have to limit
the amount of risks we write.</font></div>
      </div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #003366; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">&#160;</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #003366; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">We
cannot guarantee that our reinsurers will pay us in a timely fashion, if at
all.&#160;&#160;In addition, we remain primarily liable to our insureds, whether
our reinsurers pay or not, and therefore could experience losses.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">We
transfer a portion of the risk we have assumed under our insurance policies to
reinsurance companies in exchange for part of the premium we receive in
connection with the risk.&#160;&#160;Although reinsurance makes the reinsurer
liable to us to the extent of the risk transferred, it does not relieve us of
our liability to our policyholders.&#160;&#160;If our reinsurers fail to pay us
or fail to pay us on a timely basis, our financial condition, results of
operations or cash flow would be adversely affected.</font></div>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #003366; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Significant
changes in the healthcare delivery system, through healthcare reform or
otherwise, could materially affect our operations.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Healthcare
reform or other significant changes could alter the healthcare delivery system,
raise the cost sensitivity of our insureds, or alter how healthcare providers
insure their MPL risks. Healthcare reform legislation is pending in both houses
of the U.S. Congress, but we cannot predict which, if any, reform proposals will
be adopted, when any such proposals might take effect, or what effect they may
have on our business.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">In
addition, significant market-driven changes in the healthcare system have
resulted in many medical professionals joining or becoming contractually
affiliated with hospitals and other larger organizations.&#160;&#160;This trend
may result in a significant decrease in the role of the physician in the MPL
insurance purchasing decision and in a significant increase in the role of
professional risk managers, who may be more price-sensitive and who may favor
insurance companies that are larger and more highly rated than we are. Also,
larger healthcare organizations tend to retain more risk than independent
professionals and are more likely to self-insure. For these reasons,
consolidation in the healthcare industry could negatively affect our
business.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #003366; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Our
status as an insurance holding company with no direct operations could adversely
affect our ability to fund operations, conduct future share repurchases, or meet
our debt obligations.&#160;</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">We are
an insurance holding company.&#160;&#160;The primary source of funds available
to us for the payment of operating expenses, share repurchases and debt-related
amounts are management fees and dividends from our insurance
subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;The payment of dividends by our insurance subsidiaries
is restricted by state insurance laws.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #003366; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Any
acquisitions we make, including our acquisition of Advocate, MD, could disrupt
our business and harm our financial condition or results of
operations.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">As part
of our growth strategy, we continue to evaluate opportunities to acquire other
MPL insurers or blocks of MPL business.&#160;&#160;Our acquisition of Advocate,
MD or any other acquisitions that we may make or implement in the future entail
a number of risks that could materially adversely affect our business and
operating results, including:</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

services of any of our senior management or any other key employee, or the
inability to identify, hire and retain other highly qualified personnel in the
future, could adversely affect the quality and profitability of our business
operations.</font></div>

party rating agencies assess and rate the claims paying ability of insurers
based upon criteria established by the agencies.&#160;&#160;Financial strength
ratings are used by agents and clients as an important means of assessing the
financial strength and quality of insurers.&#160;&#160;A significant downgrade
or withdrawal of any such rating could adversely affect our ability to sell
insurance policies and inhibit us from competing effectively.&#160;&#160;In

        <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 15.95pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
        <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">We, in
common with the insurance industry in general, are subject to litigation
involving claims under our insurance policies in the normal course of
business.&#160;&#160;We may also become involved in legal actions not involving
claims under our insurance policies from time to time.&#160;&#160;We have
evaluated such exposures as of December 31, 2009, and in all cases, believe our
positions and defenses are meritorious.&#160;&#160;However, there can be no
assurance as to the outcome of such exposures.&#160;&#160;Liabilities for loss
contingencies arising from claims, assessments, litigation, fines and penalties
and other sources are recorded when it is determined to be probable that a
liability has been incurred and the amount of the assessment and/or remediation
can be reasonably estimated.</font></div>
        <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      </div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">In
addition, our insurance subsidiaries may become subject to claims for
extra-contractual obligations or risks in excess of policy limits in connection
with their insurance claims, particularly in Florida.&#160;&#160;These claims
are sometimes referred to as &#8220;bad faith&#8221; actions as it is alleged that the
insurance company acted in bad faith in the administration of a claim against an
insured.&#160;&#160;Bad faith actions are infrequent and generally occur in
instances where a jury verdict exceeds the insured&#8217;s policy
limits.&#160;&#160;Under such circumstances, it is routinely alleged that the
insurance company failed to negotiate a settlement of a claim in good faith
within the insured&#8217;s policy limit.&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: ArialMT, sans-serif">In recent years,
policy limits for MPL insurance in Florida have trended
downward.&#160;&#160;This trend and the current judicial climate have increased
the incidence and size of jury awards in excess of policy limits against Florida
medical professionals insured by our competitors and us.&#160;&#160;Such awards
could ultimately result in increased frequency of claims by insureds or
plaintiffs in MPL actions alleging bad faith on the part of Florida MPL
insurers.&#160;&#160;</font>We have evaluated such exposures as of December 31,
2009, and believe that our position and defenses are
meritorious.&#160;&#160;However, there can be no assurance as to the outcome of
such exposures.&#160;&#160;An award against us for extra-contractual liability
or a significant jury award, or series of awards, against one or more of our
insureds could ultimately result in the payment by us of potentially significant
amounts in excess of the related policy limits, reserves and reinsurance
coverage and could have a material adverse impact on our financial condition,
results of operations or cash flows.</font></div>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">For
additional information concerning our commitments and contingencies, see <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Item 7.&#160;&#160;Management&#8217;s
Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations</font>
as well as <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Note 19,
Commitments and Contingencies </font>to the consolidated financial statements
included elsewhere herein.</font></div>

offering in 1996 and presently have no plans to do so in the foreseeable
future.&#160;&#160;Any payment of dividends in the future would be subject to
the discretion of our Board of Directors, which takes into consideration such
factors as our capital adequacy and its assessment of our future capital
needs.&#160;&#160;As a holding company with no direct operations other than the
management of our subsidiaries, we would primarily rely on cash dividends and
other permitted payments from our subsidiaries to pay any future
dividends.&#160;&#160;State insurance laws limit the dividends or other amounts
that may be paid to us by our insurance subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;In addition,
under certain circumstances, limitations may be placed on our ability to pay
dividends by the terms of the indenture agreements relating to our junior
subordinated debentures.&#160;&#160;For further information, see the discussion
under the heading &#8220;Liquidity and Capital Resources&#8221; in <font color="#000000" style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: normal; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial">Item 7.&#160;&#160;Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of

            <td width="886">
