            <td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; COLOR: #1f497d; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><a name="note4">4</a>.</font></div>
            </td>
            <td>
              <div align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; COLOR: #1f497d; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Fair
      Value Measurements</font></div>
            </td>
          </tr></table>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 12.55pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Fair
value is the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a
liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the
measurement date (an exit price methodology).&#160;&#160;We utilize market data
or assumptions that we believe market participants would use in pricing the
asset or liability, including assumptions about risk and the risks inherent in
the inputs to the valuation technique.&#160;&#160;These inputs can be readily
observable, market corroborated or generally unobservable.&#160;&#160;We have
primarily applied the market approach for recurring fair value measurements and
endeavor to utilize the most important information available to
us.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, we utilize valuation techniques that maximize the
use of observable inputs and minimize the use of unobservable
inputs.&#160;&#160;We then classify fair value balances based on the
observability of those inputs.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">The
fair value hierarchy prioritizes the inputs used to measure fair
value.&#160;&#160;The fair value hierarchy gives the highest priority to quoted
prices in active markets and the lowest priority to unobservable
data.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div>
      <table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-FAMILY: arial; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-FAMILY: arial">
<tr valign="top" style="LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt;">
            <td style="WIDTH: 36pt">
              <div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;
      </font></div>
            </td>
            <td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 12pt;" face="Wingdings">&#376;</font></font></div>
            </td>
            <td>
              <div align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Quoted Prices in Active Markets
      for Identical Assets:&#160;&#160;</font>Level 1 includes unadjusted quoted
      prices for identical assets or liabilities in active
    markets.</font></div>
            </td>
          </tr></table>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div>
      <table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-FAMILY: arial; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-FAMILY: arial">
<tr valign="top" style="LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt;">
            <td style="WIDTH: 36pt">
              <div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;
      </font></div>
            </td>
            <td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 12pt;" face="Wingdings">&#376;</font></font></div>
            </td>
            <td>
              <div align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Significant Other Observable
      Inputs</font>: Level 2 includes inputs other than quoted prices included
      within Level 1 that are observable for assets or liabilities either
      directly or indirectly.&#160;&#160;Level 2 inputs include, among other
      items, quoted prices for similar assets and liabilities in active markets,
      quoted prices for identical or similar assets and liabilities in markets
      that are not active, and inputs other than quoted prices that are
      observable for the asset or liability such as interest rates and yield
      curves.</font></div>
            </td>
          </tr></table>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div>
      <table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-FAMILY: arial; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-FAMILY: arial">
<tr valign="top" style="LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt;">
            <td style="WIDTH: 36pt">
              <div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;
      </font></div>
            </td>
            <td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 12pt;" face="Wingdings">&#376;</font></font></div>
            </td>
            <td>
              <div align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Significant Unobservable
      Inputs: </font>Level 3 inputs are unobservable and reflect management&#8217;s
      judgments about assumptions that market participants would use in pricing
      an asset or liability.</font></div>
            </td>
          </tr></table>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">A
financial instrument&#8217;s categorization within the valuation hierarchy is based
upon the lowest level of input that is significant to the fair value
measurement.&#160;&#160;Reclassifications impacting Level 3 financial
instruments are reported as transfers in (out) of the Level 3 category as of the
beginning of the period in which the transfer occurs.&#160;&#160;Therefore,
gains and losses in income only reflect activity for the period the instrument
was classified in Level 3.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">The
following is a description of the valuation measurements used for our financial
instruments carried or disclosed at fair value, as well as the general
classification of such financial instruments pursuant to the valuation
hierarchy.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #1f497d; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Valuation
of Investments</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">We
primarily use a single pricing service, Interactive Data Corporation (&#8220;IDC&#8221;), to
value our investments that have an exchange traded price or multiple observable
inputs.&#160; In situations where IDC does not have multiple observable inputs
or the ability to price a given security, we seek to price the security
utilizing another pricing service or by obtaining non-binding broker / dealer
quotes.&#160;</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">

        <div style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left">
          <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
            <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><font style="DISPLAY: inline">Form </font>10-K: F-23</font></div>
          </div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">On a
quarterly basis, we obtain and review the pricing methodology of our pricing
service to ensure that our fair value designations are classified in accordance
with the fair value hierarchy.&#160;&#160;Our pricing service provides a single
price per security.&#160;&#160;We review the results of our pricing service for
reasonableness each quarter by comparing market values reported on individual
cusip basis and an overall portfolio basis to those obtained from our external
investment manager to determine that the market value reported by our pricing
service appears reasonable.&#160;&#160;In addition, an annual SAS 70 report that
describes procedures surrounding the compilation and reporting of security
prices obtained from our pricing service is provided to us.&#160;&#160;We may
adjust the valuation of securities from the independent pricing service if we
believe a security&#8217;s price does not fairly represent the market value of the
investment. &#160;For example, when market observable data is not as readily
available or if the security trades in an inactive market, the valuation of
financial instruments becomes more subjective and could involve substantial
judgment resulting in Level 3 pricing. To date, we have not adjusted any prices
supplied by our pricing service.</font></div>

securities priced by our pricing service using an exchange traded price are
designated by us as Level 1.&#160;&#160;We designate as Level 2 those securities
not actively traded on an exchange for which our pricing service utilizes
multiple verifiable observable inputs.&#160;&#160;For securities that do not
have multiple observable inputs (Level 3), we do not rely on a price from our
pricing service.</font></div>

      funds that trade in active markets, are classified within Level 1 as their
      fair value is based on quoted market prices for identical assets as of the
      reporting date. Other instruments, typically Treasury securities and
      corporate bonds, are classified in Level 2 because they trade in less
      active markets.&#160;&#160;Their fair value is based on valuation
      methodologies, the significant inputs into which include, but are not
      limited to, benchmark <font style="DISPLAY: inline">yields, reported

financial instruments</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

      <table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-FAMILY: arial; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-FAMILY: arial">
<tr valign="top" style="LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt;">
            <td style="WIDTH: 36pt">

            </td>
            <td>
              <div align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Our
      derivative instruments, principally interest rate swaps, are valued using
      models that primarily use market observable inputs and are classified as
      Level 2 as their fair value is largely based on observable inputs over the
      life of the swaps in a liquid market. The fair value of the interest rate
      swaps is calculated by comparing the stream of cash flows on the fixed
      rate debt versus the stream of cash flows that would arise under the
      floating rate debt. The floating and fixed rate cash flows are then
      discounted to the valuation date by using the three month London Interbank
      Offered Rate (&#8220;LIBOR&#8221;) at the date of the valuation.&#160;&#160;Pricing
      inputs include bid-ask spreads and current market prices for an underlying
      instrument.</font></div>
            </td>

<tr valign="top" style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12.55pt;">
            <td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; COLOR: #1f497d; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><a name="note5">5</a>.</font></div>
            </td>
            <td>
              <div align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; COLOR: #1f497d; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Fair
      Value of Financial Instruments</font></div>
            </td>
          </tr></table>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 12.55pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">The
accounting guidance on the <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Fair Value of Financial
Instruments</font>, requires the disclosure of the estimated fair value of
financial instruments including those financial instruments for which the fair
value option has not been elected.&#160;&#160;The fair values of such
instruments have been derived, in part, by management&#8217;s assumptions, the
estimated amount and timing of future cash flows and estimated discount
rates.&#160;&#160;Different assumptions could significantly affect these
estimated fair values.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, the net realizable values could
be materially different from the estimates presented below.&#160;&#160;In
addition, the estimates are only indicative of the value of individual financial
instruments and should not be considered an indication of the fair value of FPIC
as a whole.&#160;&#160;The accounting guidance does not require the disclosure
of the fair value of lease financing arrangements and nonfinancial instruments,
including goodwill and intangible assets.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

value estimates are made as of a specific point in time based on the
characteristics of the financial instruments and relevant market
information.&#160;&#160;The following methods and assumptions were used to
estimate the fair value of each class of financial instruments for which it is
practicable to estimate that value:</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; COLOR: #003366; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Other-than-temporary
impairment (&#8220;OTTI&#8221;)</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><font style="DISPLAY: inline">We separate OTTI into the following two components: (i)
the amount related to credit losses, which is recognized in the consolidated
statements of income, and (ii) the amount related to all other factors, which is
recorded in other comprehensive income (loss). The credit-related portion of an
OTTI is measured by comparing a security&#8217;s amortized cost to the present value
of its current expected cash flows discounted at its effective yield prior to
the impairment charge.&#160;&#160;Based on our understanding of the market
statistics and the deterioration in fundamentals of our other-than-temporarily
impaired securities held as of July 1, 2009, we determined that the underlying
creditworthiness of the securities to be the primary driver in considering them
to be other-than-temporarily impaired.&#160;&#160;Therefore, </font>no
other-than-temporary impairment charges were taken due to any factors other than
credit.&#160;&#160;All of our other-than-temporary impairment charges were
recognized in earnings and no transition adjustment was necessary.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">The
determination of whether unrealized losses are &#8220;other-than-temporary&#8221; requires
judgment based on subjective as well as objective factors.&#160;&#160;We
evaluate our investment portfolio on an ongoing basis to identify securities
that may be other-than-temporarily impaired.&#160;&#160;Changes in fair value
are evaluated to determine the extent to which such changes are attributable to
(i) fundamental factors specific to the issuer or (ii) market-related factors
such as interest rates or sector declines.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">The
issuer-specific factors considered in reaching the conclusion that securities
with declines are not other-than-temporary include (i) the extent and duration
of the decline in fair value, including the duration of any significant decline
in value, (ii) whether the security is current as to payments of principal and
interest, (iii) a valuation of any underlying collateral, (iv) current and
future conditions and trends for both the business and its industry, (v) changes
in cash flow assumptions for collateralized mortgage obligations (&#8220;CMOs&#8221;) and
(vi) rating agency actions. Based on our assessment of these factors, we will
make a determination as to the probability of recovering principal and interest
on the security.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">The
number and amount of securities for which we have recorded OTTI charges are
presented in the following table.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">During
our quarterly review of impaired securities for OTTI, including an analysis of
the collateral quality, anticipated cash flows, credit enhancements, default
rates, loss severities, the securities&#8217; relative position in their respective
capital structures, and credit ratings from statistical rating agencies, we
determined that certain fixed-income securities were other-than-temporarily
impaired.&#160;&#160;These securities were considered to be impaired based on
the extent and duration of the declines in their fair values and issuer-specific
fundamentals relating to (i) poor operating results and weakened financial
conditions, (ii) negative industry trends further impacted by the recent
economic decline, and (iii) a series of downgrades to their credit ratings.
Based on the factors that existed at the time of impairment, we did not believe
that these securities would recover their unrealized losses in the near
future.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">We
believe that the remaining securities having unrealized losses at December 31,
2009 were not other-than-temporarily impaired. We do not intend on selling any
of these securities and it is more likely than not that we will not be required
to sell any of these securities before the recovery of their amortized cost
basis.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">&#160;</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Losses
and LAE incurred related to the current year decreased approximately 5 percent
and 13 percent in 2009 and 2008, respectively.&#160;&#160;Our loss ratio
(defined as the ratio of net losses and LAE to net premiums earned) related to
the current year (excluding prior year development) was 71.0 percent, 67.5
percent, and 67.3 percent for 2009, 2008 and 2007, respectively.&#160;&#160;Our
current year loss ratio has increased in recent years as a result of lower
premium rates, following several years of overall favorable claims
trends.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Losses
and LAE for claims related to prior years represent the total net change in
estimates charged or credited to earnings in the current year with respect to
liabilities established in prior years.&#160;&#160;Information regarding losses
and LAE is accumulated over time and the estimates of the liability are revised
accordingly, with the change recognized in the period revisions are
made.&#160;&#160;As noted in the table above, during 2009 our loss and LAE
reserve estimates for prior years decreased $19.0 million compared to $17.0
million in 2008.&#160;&#160;The favorable prior year loss development reflects a
decline in expected ultimate losses for years prior to 2009, primarily the 2005
through 2007 accident years, as a result of improved claim trends compared to
earlier estimates, including lower incident to claim development, a lower number
of claims closed with indemnity payment and relative stability in payment
severity.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">While
we believe that our estimates for ultimate projected losses and LAE in total are
reasonable, there can be no assurance that our estimates will not change in the
future given the many variables inherent in such estimates and the extended
period of time that it can take for claim patterns to emerge.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">We
purchase reinsurance from a number of companies to mitigate concentrations of
credit risk.&#160;&#160;Our reinsurance broker assists us in the analysis of the
credit quality of our reinsurers.&#160;&#160;We base our reinsurance buying
decisions in part on an evaluation of the then current financial strength and
stability of prospective reinsurers.&#160;&#160;However, the financial strength
of our reinsurers, and their corresponding ability to pay us, may change in the
future due to forces or events we cannot control or anticipate.&#160;&#160;At
December 31, 2009 our recoverable from reinsurers, net of amounts due, was
approximately $146.2 million.&#160;&#160;We have not experienced any difficulty
in collecting amounts due from reinsurers related to the financial condition of
the reinsurer.&#160;&#160;Should future events lead us to believe that any
reinsurer is unable to meet its obligations, adjustments to the amounts
recoverable would be reflected in the results of current
operations.</font></div>

table below displays certain aspects of the coverage provided by our excess of
loss reinsurance program for First Professionals, APAC and
Intermed:</font></div>

Professionals.&#160;&#160;The corresponding net liabilities related to these
agreements carried by First Professionals totaled $103.4
million.&#160;&#160;First Professionals recognized an after-tax gain of $9.7
million as a result of the commutation.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">We
established three wholly owned, but not consolidated, trusts, FPIC Capital Trust
I, FPIC Capital Statutory Trust II and FPIC Capital Statutory Trust III, during
2003 for the sole purpose of issuing the trust-preferred
securities.&#160;&#160;The proceeds received by the three trusts were used to
purchase junior subordinated debentures from FPIC of the same amounts,
maturities and other applicable terms and features.&#160;&#160;The debentures
issued by FPIC to the three trusts are subordinated to all senior indebtedness,
including the senior notes, and are equal in standing to one
another.&#160;&#160;Issuance costs for all three offerings in the aggregate
amount of approximately $1.4 million were capitalized and are being amortized
over their respective stated maturity periods of 30 years.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">The
floating interest rate charged under the trust-preferred subordinated debentures
is adjustable quarterly with changes in the three-month LIBOR, and in the case
of the first two offerings, the maximum rate that may be charged within the
first five years is 12.5 percent.&#160;&#160;We purchased hedging instruments
designed to fix the ultimate floating rate interest cost on our
indebtedness.&#160;&#160;For additional information on our hedging instruments,
see <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Note 11, Derivative
Instruments and Hedging Activities.&#160;&#160;</font>The trust-preferred
securities contain features that allow us the option, under certain conditions,
to defer interest payments for up to 20 quarters.&#160;&#160;The securities have
stated maturities of 30 years and are due in May and October 2033.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Indenture
agreements, relating to our junior subordinated debentures and trust-preferred
securities, contain limitations, under certain circumstances, as to (i) the
declaration or payment of dividends, or distributions thereon, or the
redemption, purchase, acquisition or liquidation with respect to any capital
stock of FPIC or its affiliates; (ii) the payment, in certain circumstances, of
principal of, premium or interest on, or the repayment, repurchase or redemption
of, debt securities of FPIC or its affiliates that rank in equal standing with
or are junior in interest to the debentures; or (iii) the payment, in certain
circumstances, under any guarantees of FPIC or its affiliates that rank equal in
standing with or junior in interest to capital securities guarantees relating to
the issuance of the debentures. Circumstances that would result in such
limitations include a continuing event of default, as defined by the indenture
agreements, a default with respect to payment of any obligations under capital
securities guarantees, or a continuing interest deferral election made by
FPIC.</font></div>

<tr valign="top" style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12.55pt;">
            <td style="WIDTH: 36pt">
              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; COLOR: #1f497d; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><a name="note11">11.</a></font></div>
            </td>
            <td>
              <div align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; COLOR: #1f497d; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Derivative
      Instruments and Hedging Activities</font></div>
            </td>
          </tr></table>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 12.55pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Prior
to May and November 2008, our derivative instruments consisted of four interest
rate collars.&#160;&#160;The interest rate collars were designated as cash flow
hedges and reflected at fair value in our consolidated statement of financial
position.&#160;&#160;The interest rate collars were designed to maintain our
ultimate floating rate interest costs on our trust-preferred securities and
unsecured senior notes within a specified interest range for up to five years
from the closing date of those liabilities.&#160;&#160;The interest rate collars
place floors and caps on the three-month LIBOR floating interest on notional
principal corresponding with the principal amounts of each offering, until their
respective maturity dates in 2008.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Under
the interest rate collars, when the three-month LIBOR interest rate exceeded the
specified cap rate or fell below the specified floor rate, we received or paid,
respectively, the related cash flow equal to the difference in the interest rate
times the notional principal amount under the respective
contracts.&#160;&#160;The two portions of each contract working together,
therefore, formed a hedge against the effects of a rising three-month LIBOR rate
above the cap or a falling three-month LIBOR rate below the
floor.&#160;&#160;The notional amounts of the contract were not
exchanged.&#160;&#160;Therefore, the excess of the interest expense on our
securities over the cap rate, or the shortfall in interest expense under the
floor, were offset by related receipts of excess interest above the caps, or the
payment of the interest shortfall below the floor, respectively.&#160;&#160;No
other cash payments were made.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">The
interest rate collars and terms are presented in the table below with their
corresponding effects on the floating rate interest costs associated with the
trust-preferred securities and senior notes.</font></div>

              <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: arial, sans-serif">(1)</font></div>
            </td>
            <td align="left" valign="top" width="70%">
              <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: arial, sans-serif">Based
      on the three month LIBOR.</font></div>
            </td>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">

          <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
            <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><font style="DISPLAY: inline">Form </font>10-K: F-38</font></div>

        <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;

      <div id="HDR">
        <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 9pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman"><a href="#tocindex">Table of Contents</a></font></div>
        <div style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left">
          <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 15.95pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 14pt; COLOR: #003366; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, serif">FPIC
Insurance Group, Inc.</font></div>
          <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 15.95pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Notes
to the Consolidated Financial Statements</font></div>
          <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 0pt">
            <div>
              <hr style="COLOR: #003366" align="left" noshade size="1" width="100%">
            </div><br></div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">During
May and November 2008, we replaced our expiring interest rate collars and
effected new interest rate swaps to hedge the floating interest rate risk on our
outstanding indebtedness.&#160;&#160;We use hedging contracts to manage the risk
of our exposure to interest rate changes associated with our variable rate debt.
All of our designated hedging instruments are considered to be cash flow
hedges.&#160;&#160;Our derivative transactions represent a hedge of specified
cash flows.&#160;&#160;As a result, these interest rate swaps are derivatives
and were designated as cash flow hedging instruments at the initiation of the
swaps.&#160;&#160;We formally document qualifying hedged transactions and
hedging instruments, and assess, both at inception of the contract and on an
ongoing basis, whether the hedging instruments are effective in offsetting
changes in cash flows of the hedged transaction.&#160;&#160;At the end of each
period, the interest rate swaps are recorded in the consolidated statement of
financial position at fair value, in other assets if the hedge is an asset
position, or in other liabilities if it is in a liability position. Any related
increases or decreases in fair value are recognized in our consolidated
statement of financial position in accumulated other comprehensive income
(loss).</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">We
consider our interest rate swaps to be a Level 2 measurement under the fair
value hierarchy, as their fair value is largely based on observable inputs over
the life of the swaps in a liquid market. The fair value of the interest rate
swaps is calculated by comparing the stream of cash flows on the fixed rate debt
versus the stream of cash flows that would arise under the floating rate debt.
The floating and fixed rate cash flows are then discounted to the valuation date
by using the three month LIBOR rate at the date of the valuation.&#160;&#160;The
valuation of the interest rate swap can be sensitive to changes in current and
future three month LIBOR rates, which can have a material impact on the fair
value of the derivatives. However, as these swaps are used to manage our cash
outflows, these changes will not materially impact our liquidity and capital
resources.&#160;&#160;Furthermore, since the interest rate swaps are deemed as
effective hedging instruments, these changes do not impact income from
operations.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; COLOR: #003366; FONT-STYLE: italic">Interest
rate risk.&#160;&#160;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline">We are exposed to
interest rate risk associated with fluctuations in the interest rates on our
variable interest rate debt.&#160;&#160;In order to manage this risk, we have
entered into several interest rate swaps that convert the debt's variable rate
debt to fixed rate debt.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2009, we had long-term
debt obligations of $46.1 million, comprised of $10.0 million in senior notes
and $36.1 million in junior subordinated debentures.&#160;&#160;Our long-term
debt obligations are uncollateralized and bear floating interest at rates equal
to the three-month LIBOR plus an interest rate spread.&#160;&#160;Our floating
interest rates are adjusted quarterly.&#160;&#160;We are required during the
swap terms to make certain fixed rate payments to the counterparty calculated on
the notional amount in exchange for receiving floating payments based on the
three-month LIBOR for the same amount.&#160;&#160;The notional amounts on the
contracts are not exchanged.&#160;&#160;The net effect of this accounting on our
operating results is that interest expense on our floating rate indebtedness is
recorded based on fixed interest rates.</font></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; COLOR: #003366; FONT-STYLE: italic">Credit
risk</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; COLOR: #003366">.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline">&#160;&#160;By using interest rate-related derivative
instruments to manage the exposure on our variable rate debt, we expose
ourselves to credit risk.&#160;&#160;We are exposed to potential losses if the
counterparty fails to perform according to the terms of its
agreement.&#160;&#160;When the fair value of a derivative contract is positive
(in a net asset position), the counterparty owes us, which may present a credit
risk for us.&#160;&#160;We manage our exposure to credit risk by entering into
transactions with well-established financial institutions and by monitoring the
financial strength ratings and financial developments of such
institutions.&#160;&#160;In addition, only conventional derivative financial
instruments are utilized.</font></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">The
terms of our derivative agreements require that we furnish collateral in the
event that mark-to-market calculations result in settlement obligations owed by
us to the counterparties in excess of $0.8 million.&#160;&#160;No other cash
payments are made unless the swaps are terminated prior to maturity, in which
case the amount paid or received at settlement is established by agreement at
the time of termination, and usually represents the net present value, at
current interest rates, of the remaining obligations to exchange payments under
the terms of the contracts.&#160;&#160;In accordance with the accounting
guidance for offsetting of receivables and payables and as allowed under our
master netting arrangement with our counterparty, we have offset the fair value
amounts recognized in the statement of financial position for our derivative
instruments against the fair value amounts recognized for our right to reclaim
cash collateral (a receivable).&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2009 and 2008, the
cash collateral paid to our counterparty was $2.3 million and $2.9 million,
respectively.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; COLOR: #003366; FONT-STYLE: italic">Assessment
of hedge effectiveness</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; COLOR: #003366">.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline">&#160;&#160;We assess the effectiveness of our interest
rate swaps on a quarterly basis.&#160;&#160;We have considered the impact of
credit market conditions in assessing the risk of counterparty
default.&#160;&#160;We believe that it is likely that the counterparty for these
swaps will continue to act throughout the contract period, and as a result
continue to deem the swaps as effective hedging instruments.&#160;&#160;We will
perform subsequent assessments of hedge effectiveness by verifying and
documenting whether the critical terms of the hedging instrument and the
forecasted transaction have changed during the period, rather than by
quantifying the relevant changes in cash flows.&#160;&#160;Based on the fact
that, at inception, the critical terms of the hedging instruments and the hedged
forecasted transaction were the same, we have concluded that we expect changes
in cash flows attributable to the risk being hedged to be completely offset by
the hedging derivatives and have assessed that our cash flow hedges have no
ineffectiveness, as determined by the hypothetical derivative
method.&#160;&#160;If the hedge on any of the interest rate swaps was deemed
ineffective, or extinguished by either party, any accumulated gains or losses
remaining in other comprehensive income would be fully recorded in interest
expense during the period.</font></font></div>

        <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 9pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman"><a href="#tocindex">Table of Contents</a></font></div>
        <div style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left">
          <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 15.95pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 14pt; COLOR: #003366; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman, serif">FPIC
Insurance Group, Inc.</font></div>
          <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 15.95pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Notes
to the Consolidated Financial Statements</font></div>
          <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 0pt">

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt">&#160;</div>
    <div>
      <table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-FAMILY: arial; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-FAMILY: arial">
<tr valign="top" style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12.55pt;">
            <td style="WIDTH: 36pt">
              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; COLOR: #1f497d; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><a name="note15">15.</a></font></div>
            </td>
            <td>
              <div align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; COLOR: #1f497d; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Share-Based
      Compensation Plans</font></div>
            </td>
          </tr></table>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 12.55pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">We
maintain three share-based compensation plans: (i) a plan for officers and key
employees (the &#8220;Omnibus Plan&#8221;); (ii) a plan for non-employee directors (the
&#8220;Director Plan&#8221;); and (iii) an employee stock purchase plan (the
&#8220;ESPP&#8221;).&#160;&#160;We intend to issue new shares for share issuances under
these plans. In the past, we have repurchased shares of our common stock to
offset the dilutive effect of shares issued in connection with our share-based
compensation plans.&#160;&#160;Under our stock repurchase program, we may
repurchase shares at such times, and in such amounts, as management deems
appropriate, up to the maximum number of shares authorized for
repurchase.&#160;&#160;Additional details on our three plans
follows:</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; COLOR: #003366">The Omnibus Plan
-</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; COLOR: #003366; FONT-STYLE: italic">&#160;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline">Under the Omnibus Plan, we may issue stock options (both
non-qualified stock options and incentive stock options), contingent stock
(including performance-based awards), restricted stock and stock appreciation
rights upon approval by the Compensation Committee of our Board of
Directors.&#160;&#160;Awards made under the Omnibus Plan in 2007 and prior years
have consisted only of stock options and restricted stock.&#160;&#160;The
exercise price of a stock option may generally not be less than 100 percent of
the fair market value of the underlying shares on the date of
grant.&#160;&#160;During 2008 and 2009 we made grants of contingent stock with
performance-based measures and restricted stock.&#160;&#160;The contingent stock
has a two-year performance period.&#160;&#160;The final determination of the
number of shares to be issued in respect of an award (which can vary between 50
and 150 percent of the number of performance units subject to the award,
provided a threshold performance level is achieved) is determined by the
Compensation Committee of our Board of Directors.&#160;&#160;The restricted
stock grants are time based and vest in equal amounts over a three-year period,
subject to forfeiture restrictions.&#160;&#160;Restricted stock becomes
unrestricted as the awards vest.&#160;&#160;Time-vested awards made under the
Omnibus Plan generally vest over a three-year period, which represents the
requisite service period for such awards.&#160;&#160;Performance-based awards
vest upon meeting the related performance objective.&#160;&#160;Under the plan,
individuals who receive a restricted stock award are permitted to redeem an
adequate number of shares from such award upon vesting to satisfy any tax
withholding liability.&#160;&#160;Awards are generally made
annually.</font></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; COLOR: #003366">The Director Plan
-</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; COLOR: #003366; FONT-STYLE: italic">&#160;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline">Under the Director Plan, we may issue non-qualified
stock options, contingent stock, restricted stock and stock appreciation rights
upon approval by the Board of Directors.&#160;&#160;Stock option grants made
under the Director Plan are at a price not less than 100 percent of the fair
market value of the underlying stock on the grant date.&#160;&#160;Shares of
restricted stock become unrestricted as the awards vest.</font></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">The
Board of Directors has authorized annual awards pursuant to the Director Plan to
each non-employee member of the Board of Directors, as of the date of the annual
shareholders meeting, of 1,000 shares of restricted stock, which will fully vest
on the first anniversary of the date of grant, which represents the requisite
service period for such awards.&#160;&#160;The Board of Directors has also
authorized awards pursuant to the Director Plan to new non-employee directors,
upon their initial election, of 1,000 shares of restricted stock, which will
fully vest on the first anniversary of the date of grant, which represents the
requisite service period for such awards.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; COLOR: #003366">The ESPP
-</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; COLOR: #003366; FONT-STYLE: italic">&#160;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline">We offer the ESPP to eligible employees, including
executive officers.&#160;&#160;Under the terms of the ESPP, employees are
allowed to purchase up to a maximum dollar amount of FPIC&#8217;s common stock at 85
percent of the market value as of the first or last day of the offering period,
whichever is lower.&#160;&#160;FPIC common stock issued in connection with the
ESPP for the plan year ended December 31, 2009 totaled 4,486
shares.</font></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">We use
historical data and projections to estimate expected employee behavior related
to stock award exercises and forfeitures.&#160;&#160;We estimate the fair value
of each stock option on the grant date using the Black-Scholes valuation model
incorporating the assumptions noted in the following table.&#160;&#160;The fair
value of restricted stock awards, including performance units, is based on the
closing sales price of FPIC common stock on the date of
issuance.&#160;&#160;Stock valuation models require the input of highly
subjective assumptions.&#160;&#160;Expected volatility and dividends are based
on historical factors related to our common stock.&#160;&#160;Expected term
represents the estimated weighted-average time between grant and employee
exercise.&#160;&#160;The risk-free rate is based on U.S. Treasury rates
appropriate for the expected term.</font></div>

          <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 15.95pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Notes

      <table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-FAMILY: arial; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-FAMILY: arial">
<tr valign="top" style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12.55pt;">
            <td style="WIDTH: 36pt">
              <div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; COLOR: #1f497d; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><a name="note16">16.</a></font></div>
            </td>
            <td>
              <div align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; COLOR: #1f497d; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Employee
      Benefit Plans</font></div>
            </td>
          </tr></table>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 12.55pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">We
provide pension benefits to eligible employees through various defined
contribution and defined benefit plans, which we sponsor.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; COLOR: #003366">Defined Contribution
Plans -</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; COLOR: #003366; FONT-STYLE: italic">&#160;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline">We have defined contribution plans that are available to
employees upon meeting certain eligibility requirements.&#160;&#160;The plans
allow employees to contribute to the plan a percentage of their pre-tax annual
compensation.&#160;&#160;Under the terms of the plans, we will match the
employee contributions up to a maximum of 2.5 percent of the employee&#8217;s annual
compensation.&#160;&#160;We may also make annual profit sharing contributions to
the plans, depending on annual financial performance.&#160;&#160;The
contributions to the plans are invested at the election of the employee in one
or more investment options provided by a third party plan
administrator.&#160;&#160;Our contributions to the plans totaled $0.9 million,
$1.2 million and $1.5 million for the years ended December 31, 2009, 2008 and
2007, respectively.&#160;&#160;We expect to contribute approximately $0.9
million to the defined contribution plan during 2010.</font></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><font style="DISPLAY: inline">We have a deferred compensation plan, which is offered
to key employees selected by the Board of Directors.&#160;&#160;Key employee
participants may defer into the plan all or a portion of their
compensation.&#160;&#160;In addition, at the discretion of the Board of
Directors, we may match contributions made by key employees and may make
discretionary incentive contributions for key
employees.&#160;&#160;Participants&#8217; account balances generally will be paid, as
adjusted for investment gains or losses, following termination of
employment.&#160;&#160;See the discussion below entitled </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; COLOR: #003366; FONT-STYLE: italic">Defined Benefit Plan
Curtailment</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline"> for additional details on the
deferred compensation plan liability as of December 31, 2008.&#160;&#160;During
the years ended December 31, 2007 and 2008, we did not make any discretionary or
matching contributions to the plan.&#160;&#160;We made a contribution of less
than $2.2 million to the deferred compensation plan during the year ended
December 31, 2009, including $2.1 million related to the</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; COLOR: #003366; FONT-STYLE: italic">&#160;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Defined Benefit Plan
Curtailment</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline">.&#160;&#160;We expect to
contribute approximately $0.3 million to the deferred compensation plan during
2010.</font></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">We have
a money purchase plan that is available to the employees of Tenere upon meeting
certain eligibility requirements.&#160;&#160;Under the terms of the plan, we
contribute to the plan to provide benefits to employees based on years of
service.&#160;&#160;Contributions are made for each year of service until the
employee retires.&#160;&#160;The contributions are equal to 6.0 percent of the
employee&#8217;s annual compensation plus 5.7 percent of the employee&#8217;s annual
compensation in excess of the Social Security taxable wage base.&#160;&#160;Our
contributions totaled $0.07 million for the years ended December 31, 2009, 2008
and 2007.&#160;&#160;We expect to contribute $0.07 million to this money
purchase plan during 2010.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; COLOR: #003366">Defined Benefit Plans
-</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; COLOR: #003366; FONT-STYLE: italic">&#160;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline">We have a defined benefit plan that is available to
employees upon meeting certain eligibility requirements.&#160;&#160;During 2008
there was also a supplemental executive retirement plan (&#8220;SERP&#8221;) available only
to selected executives and an excess benefit plan (&#8220;Excess Plan&#8221;) available only
to certain employees who were not covered by the SERP.&#160;&#160;The SERP and
excess benefit plan are not funded.</font></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; COLOR: #003366; FONT-STYLE: italic">Defined Benefit Plan
</font><a name="jump_exp_4"><!--EFPlaceholder-->
</a><font style="DISPLAY: inline; COLOR: #003366; FONT-STYLE: italic">Curtailment</font>.&#160;&#160;In
December 2008, FPIC froze the accrual of future benefits under its Excess Plan
and SERP causing a <a name="jump_exp_1"><!--EFPlaceholder-->
</a>curtailment of the
plans.&#160;&#160;Given that the plans are frozen, no current or future
employees are eligible for participation.&#160;&#160;In return for the
termination of future benefits under the plans, we entered into agreements with
certain executives where we will make contributions on their behalf to our
deferred compensation plan.&#160;&#160;The contribution amounts will be
determined as a percentage of the executive&#8217;s base salary as defined in the
agreements.&#160;&#160;A liability to the deferred compensation plan in the
amount $2.1 million was recorded as of December 31, 2008.&#160;&#160;The
liability was subsequently paid during January 2009.&#160;&#160;The impact of
the curtailment and settlement on the Company&#8217;s Excess Plan and SERP is
indicated in the tables below.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">It is
our policy to contribute amounts sufficient to meet minimum funding requirements
of our defined benefit plan as set forth in employee benefit and tax laws plus
such additional amounts as may be determined to be appropriate.&#160;&#160;The
contributions to these plans totaled $0.3 million and $1.9 million for the years
ended December 31, 2009 and 2007, respectively.&#160;&#160;We did not contribute
to these plans during 2008.&#160;&#160;We expect to contribute approximately
$0.3 million to the defined benefit plan during 2010.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">The
investment policy for our defined benefit plan involves employing a sufficient
level of flexibility to capture investment opportunities as they occur, while
maintaining reasonable parameters to ensure that prudence and care are exercised
in the execution of the investment programs.&#160;&#160;We employ a total return
on investment approach, whereby a mix of equity securities, debt securities and
cash is targeted to maximize the long-term return on assets for a given level of
risk.&#160;&#160;Investment risk is measured and monitored on an ongoing basis
by plan trustees through periodic portfolio reviews and annual liability
measurements.&#160;&#160;We do not expect significant changes in the allocation
of investments; however the allocations may change after the periodic meetings
of the plan trustees based on their reviews of historical investment return and
risk.</font></div>

common with the insurance industry in general, are subject to litigation
involving claims under our insurance policies in the normal course of
business.&#160;&#160;We may also become involved in legal actions not involving
claims under our insurance policies from time to time.&#160;&#160;We have
evaluated such exposures as of December 31, 2009, and in all cases, believe our
positions and defenses are meritorious.&#160;&#160;However, there can be no
assurance as to the outcome of such exposures.&#160;&#160;Liabilities for loss
contingencies arising from claims, assessments, litigation, fines and penalties
and other sources are recorded when it is determined to be probable that a
liability has been incurred and the amount of the assessment and/or remediation
can be reasonably estimated.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">In
addition, our insurance subsidiaries may become subject to claims for
extra-contractual obligations or risks in excess of policy limits in connection
with their insurance claims, particularly in Florida.&#160;&#160;These claims
are sometimes referred to as &#8220;bad faith&#8221; actions as it is alleged that the
insurance company acted in bad faith in the administration of a claim against an
insured.&#160;&#160;Bad faith actions are infrequent and generally occur in
instances where a jury verdict exceeds the insured&#8217;s policy
limits.&#160;&#160;Under such circumstances, it is routinely alleged that the
insurance company failed to negotiate a settlement of a claim in good faith
within the insured&#8217;s policy limit.&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: ArialMT, sans-serif">In recent years,
policy limits for MPL insurance in Florida have trended
downward.&#160;&#160;This trend and the current judicial climate have increased
the incidence and size of jury awards in excess of policy limits against Florida
medical professionals insured by our competitors and us.&#160;&#160;Such awards
could ultimately result in increased frequency of claims by insureds or
plaintiffs in MPL actions alleging bad faith on the part of Florida MPL
insurers.&#160;&#160;</font>We have evaluated such exposures as of December 31,
2009, and believe our position and defenses are meritorious.
.&#160;&#160;However, there can be no assurance as to the outcome of such
exposures. An award against us for extra-contractual liability or a significant
jury award, or series of awards, against one or more of our insureds could
ultimately result in the payment by us of potentially significant amounts in
excess of the related policy limits, reserves and reinsurance coverage and could
have a material adverse impact on our financial condition, results of operations
or cash flows.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">Our
insurance subsidiaries are subject to assessment by the insurance guaranty
associations in the states in which they conduct business for the provision of
funds necessary for the settlement of covered claims under certain policies of
insolvent insurers.&#160;&#160;Generally, these associations can assess member
insurers on the basis of written premiums in their particular
states.&#160;&#160;Between 2006 and 2009, we were assessed an aggregate of $14.8
million (including $1.2 million in 2009) by the Florida Office of Insurance
Regulation (&#8220;Florida OIR&#8221;) at the request of the Florida Insurance Guaranty
Association (&#8220;FIGA&#8221;) with respect to the insolvency of property and casualty
insurance companies operating in Florida.&#160;&#160;Losses in excess of FIGA&#8217;s
estimates could result in the need for additional assessments by
FIGA.&#160;&#160;Such additional assessments or assessments related to other
property and casualty insurers that have or may become insolvent because of
hurricane activity or otherwise could adversely impact our financial condition,
results of operations or cash flows.&#160;&#160;Under Florida law, our insurance
subsidiaries are entitled to recoup insurance guaranty fund assessments from
their Florida policyholders and will continue to do so until fully
recovered.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif">In
addition to standard guaranty fund assessments, the Florida, Texas and Missouri
legislatures could also levy special assessments to settle claims caused by
certain catastrophic losses.&#160;&#160;No such special assessments for
catastrophic losses were made in 2009, 2008 or 2007.&#160;&#160;Medical
malpractice policies have been exempted from assessment by the Florida Hurricane
Catastrophe Fund until the expiration of this exemption on May 31,
2010.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; LINE-HEIGHT: 11.4pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial, sans-serif"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; COLOR: #003366">Insurance Management
-&#160;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline">Our insurance management operations
were comprised of our subsidiaries in New York and Pennsylvania that provided
insurance management services to other MPL insurers.&#160;&#160;The aggregate
purchase price for these operations was $39.1 million in cash, which reflects
cash proceeds of $40.0 million and a post-closing working capital adjustment of
$0.9 million.&#160;&#160;In connection with this transaction, we also received
approximately $5.9 million in cash from these operations prior to the
sale.&#160;&#160;We recognized an $11.6 million after-tax gain on disposition of
these operations in 2006.&#160;&#160;During the third quarter of 2007, we
recorded a loss on the sale of these operations of $0.2 million related to the
finalization of our 2006 tax return, which reflected the sale of our former
insurance management operations.</font></font></div>

January 15, 2010, we declared a three-for-two stock split of our common shares
in the form of a 50 percent stock dividend payable on March 8, 2010 to
shareholders of record as of the close of business on February 8, 2010 (the
record date).&#160;&#160;Fractional shares will be settled in cash based on the
average of the high and low sale prices for FPIC common stock reported on the
NASDAQ Stock Market on the record date.&#160;&#160;The consolidated statements
of financial position as of December 31, 2009 and 2008 have not been
retroactively restated.&#160;&#160;The table below shows our historical earnings
per share and the pro forma effect of the stock split.</font></div>
